questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

What is the domain of the relation (2,5), (4,9), (6,13)?

feedback.text: The domain is the set of input values, or x-values.
These are output values, so they form the range.
This combines inputs and outputs instead of isolating the domain.
This mixes inputs with outputs and leaves out values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

What is the range of the relation (2,5), (4,9), (6,13)?

feedback.text: These are input values, so they form the domain.
This combines every value. The range includes only outputs.
The range is the set of output values, or y-values.
This includes one input and omits one output.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

A table has inputs -1, 0, 1, 2 and outputs 7, 4, 1, -2. What is the domain?

feedback.text: These are outputs, so they form the range.
The domain is the set of inputs.
This is the range written in increasing order, not the domain.
This mixes inputs and outputs.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

A graph has points (0,3), (1,5), and (2,7). What is the range?

feedback.text: These are the x-values, so they form the domain.
This lists both inputs and outputs.
This is not the set of y-values shown by the points.
The range is the set of y-values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

Which set is a reasonable domain for the number of students in a classroom?

feedback.text: A count of students must be a nonnegative whole number.
A student count cannot include fractions or negative values.
A classroom cannot have a negative number of students.
Student counts are whole-number counts, not decimals.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

A runner tracks distance from 0 to 5 miles during a workout. Which range is reasonable for the distance run?

feedback.text: The runner has distances less than 5 before finishing.
The distance can start at 0, end at 5, and include values between.
Distances in this context cannot be negative or exceed the workout distance.
The workout is capped at 5 miles.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

For the ordered pairs (-3,8), (-1,4), and (1,0), which set is the domain?

feedback.text: These are output values, so they form the range.
This combines input and output values.
This mixes an input with output values.
The x-values are -3, -1, and 1.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

A function gives the cost C(n) for buying n notebooks. Which domain is reasonable?

feedback.text: Notebook counts cannot be negative or fractional in this purchase context.
Negative integers are not reasonable counts of notebooks.
A person cannot buy a decimal part of a notebook in this count model.
The input is a nonnegative whole-number count.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

What is the range of the relation (5,1), (6,1), (7,2)?

feedback.text: Repeated output values are listed once in the range.
These are x-values, so they form the domain.
Sets do not repeat identical values.
This combines domain and range values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

A table shows inputs 1, 2, 3, 4 and outputs 12, 10, 8, 6. Which statement is correct?

feedback.text: Those values are outputs, so they form the range.
Those values are inputs, so they form the domain.

answer.text: The domain and range are the same set.

feedback.text: The input and output sets are different.
The domain is the set of input values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

Which range is reasonable for the height of water in a tank that can be filled from 0 inches to 48 inches?

feedback.text: The height cannot be negative or exceed 48 inches in this context.
The height can be any amount from empty to full.
The tank can be partially filled.
Values greater than 48 inches exceed the tank height.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

What is the domain of the relation (0,-2), (3,-2), and (6,-2)?

feedback.text: This is the only output value, so it is the range.
This combines domain and range values.
The domain is the set of x-values.
This leaves out two input values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

What is the range of the relation (0,-2), (3,-2), and (6,-2)?

feedback.text: The only output value is -2, and repeated values are listed once.
These are input values, so they form the domain.
This combines inputs and outputs.
A set lists repeated values only once.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

A vending machine function uses d for the number of dollars inserted. If the machine accepts only whole dollar bills from 0 to 10, which domain is reasonable?

feedback.text: The machine accepts only whole dollar bills, so decimals are not reasonable inputs.
Negative integers and values above 10 are outside the context.
The input values are whole-dollar amounts from 0 through 10.
The machine may accept amounts less than 10.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

Which statement best describes the domain of a function?

feedback.text: That describes the range, not the domain.
A domain is a set of inputs, not a single output.

answer.text: The rule used to calculate outputs

feedback.text: The rule defines the function, while the domain describes allowed inputs.
The domain is the set of input values for a function.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

Which statement best describes the range of a function?

feedback.text: That describes the domain.
The range is the set of output values.
Range is based on output values, which are usually y-values.
The independent variable is connected to inputs, not outputs.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

The points (1,10), (2,20), (3,30), and (4,40) are shown on a graph. Which set is the range?

feedback.text: The range is the set of y-values.
These are x-values, so they form the domain.
This combines x-values and y-values.
This leaves out one output value.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

A function models the cost of buying movie tickets. Which output unit should appear in the range?

feedback.text: Tickets are the input count in this context.
The output of a cost function is measured in dollars.
Time is not the output unit in this ticket cost context.
The function models cost, not a number of people.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

For a function that gives temperature over a 24-hour day, which domain is reasonable if t is measured in hours after midnight?

feedback.text: The context limits time to one 24-hour day.
This misses possible times such as 2.5 hours after midnight.
Time can vary continuously from the start to the end of the day.
Those are output-type values, not time inputs.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

What is the domain of the relation shown by x-values 4, 8, 12 and y-values 1, 3, 5?

feedback.text: These are y-values, so they form the range.
This combines input and output values.
The domain is the set of x-values.
This mixes inputs and outputs and omits values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

For the ordered pairs (1, 4), (2, 6), and (3, 8), what is the domain?

feedback.text: This is the range.
This mixes input and output values.
This omits inputs and includes outputs.
The domain is the set of input or x-values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

For the ordered pairs (1, 4), (2, 6), and (3, 8), what is the range?

feedback.text: This is the domain.
This mixes an input with output values.
The range is the set of output or y-values.
This mixes input and output values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

Which values belong in the domain of a function?

feedback.text: The domain is the set of all allowed inputs.
Output values make up the range.
The domain can include many kinds of input values.
Zero may or may not be in the domain.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

A context allows only whole-number numbers of tickets: 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4. What is the domain?

feedback.text: The context restricts the input to whole-number ticket counts shown.
The domain is the allowed ticket counts.
All listed ticket counts are allowed, not just the largest.
Costs are outputs, not the domain.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U04_L04_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.FN.1

Why can context restrict a domain?

answer.text: Context always makes the domain empty

feedback.text: Most contexts still allow reasonable inputs.

answer.text: The range must always equal the domain

feedback.text: Domain and range do not need to be equal.

answer.text: Some input values may not make sense in the situation

feedback.text: For example, negative tickets or fractional people may not be meaningful.

answer.text: The graph decides without using the situation

feedback.text: The situation helps determine realistic input values.
